strategic_themes.title: Lift qualified audit opinion (Forvis Mazars LLP)
strategic_themes.rationale: External auditor issued a qualified opinion on 2024/25 statements. Direct: PSAA scale fee normalisation. Indirect: lifting governance flag reduces borrowing-cost premium. Manual read of audit report needed to itemise qualification reason — once known, target single-cycle remediation.

strategic_themes.title: Agency / locum staff demand reduction (£4M concentrated)
strategic_themes.rationale: £4M of agency-staff spend across 1 master vendors. Top: COMENSURA LTD (£4M). Standard transformation: cap agency premium at 20% above substantive rate, workforce-plan permanent conversion (6-9 month payback), regional bank pool, open-book master-vendor margins. CIPFA experience: 8-15% reduction in 12-18 months.
strategic_themes.decision_owner: Director of HR + Director of Finance + S151 Officer

strategic_themes.title: Energy procurement via CCS / LASER / NEPO frameworks (£74M baseline)
strategic_themes.rationale: £74M utility spend across 5 suppliers. Top: EDF ENERGY CUSTOMERS PLC (£40M), EDF ENERGY CUSTOMERS LTD (£16M), CORONA ENERGY RETAIL 2 LTD (£15M), SSE UTILITY SOLUTIONS LTD (£2M), NPOWER NORTHERN LTD (£1M). Crown Commercial RM6306 + LASER / NEPO consortium flex purchase typically saves 4-8% vs direct supplier contracts on a 3-yr horizon. Plus solar PV self-generation on council estate (7-9 yr payback) + DESNZ Public Sector Decarbonisation Scheme grants up to 100% capex on heat pump conversion.
strategic_themes.decision_owner: Director of Property + Sustainability Lead + S151 Officer

strategic_themes.title: Treasury management + borrowing cost optimisation (CFR proxy £399M)
strategic_themes.rationale: Annual revenue £499M implies indicative CFR c. £399M. Standard levers: internal borrowing from earmarked reserves, PWLB Certainty Rate trade, MMF counterparty restructuring, LGPS Property Investment Pool inclusion. 10-30bp saving on external debt typical from a fresh review.

strategic_themes.title: LGPS employer contribution opportunity (2025 triennial valuation cycle)
strategic_themes.rationale: Indicative pay bill £200M × c. 22% employer contribution rate = £44M annual employer contribution. Most LGPS funds materially over-funded post-2022 (returns 2022-25 averaged 7-10% pa vs 3-4% discount-rate assumption). 2025 triennial valuation typically yields 2-4pp employer-rate reduction over 2026-2029. Confirm with administering authority + actuary.

strategic_themes.title: Fees, charges + traded-services income optimisation (£50M base)
strategic_themes.rationale: Indicative fees & charges + traded-services income c. 10% of revenue = £50M. Standard levers: annual CPI uplift discipline, full-cost-recovery audit on discretionary services (parking, planning, licensing, sports, adult learning, property hire), commercial pricing on traded services. LGA experience: 5-15% income uplift sustainable over 2-3 years.

strategic_themes.title: Insurance retention + premium review (£0.5M premium estimate)
strategic_themes.rationale: Indicative insurance premium £0.5M (10bp of revenue). Standard 3-5 yr renewal cycle. Levers: tender via IPG / RM Partners (10-25% premium reduction typical), retention review (increase excess + build risk-fund reserve). London-borough cohort average 12% premium reduction at last tender.

strategic_themes.title: Contracts Finder portfolio review (98 notices; 8 contracts at £10M+ ceiling)
strategic_themes.rationale: Contracts Finder data: 98 notices (57 awarded, £90M aggregate ADVERTISED CEILING value, 0% SME). IMPORTANT: advertised contract value is a CEILING set to avoid retender risk under PCR 2015 Reg.72 / Procurement Act 2023 s.31 — actual spend through the awardee is typically 30-70% of ceiling, with some off-contract ledger spend permitted within the 50%/50% modification limits. 8 contracts at £10M+ ceiling totalling £1344M (ceiling, NOT spend) — top 3: The appointment of a Technology Partner and the establishmen (ceiling £500M); The appointment of a Technology Partner and the establishmen (ceiling £500M); Sunderland Central Heat Network (ceiling £130M). Matched against ledger: Drainage Investigation and Maintenance Framework — ceiling £3.6M, actual ledger spend with awardee £20.3M; Framework for the Provision of Security Guarding a — ceiling £7.5M, actual ledger spend with awardee £7.7M; Portable Toilet Units and Accessible Portable Unit — ceiling £0.1M, actual ledger spend with awardee £2.3M. Aggregate identified actual spend £862M. SME-awarded share 0% is below the Procurement Reform 2023 / PPN 03/24 ambition (33% SME share by value). Standard procurement-data savings levers (% of ACTUAL ledger spend, not ceiling): (a) modification-history scrutiny under PCR 2015 Reg.72, (b) Procurement Act 2023 s.31 contract change notice review, (c) re-tender benchmark vs CCS framework rates on next renewal. 2-8% on actual spend through major contracts is a defensible upper bound.
strategic_themes.decision_owner: Head of Procurement + Cabinet Member + Section 151 Officer

strategic_themes.title: Companies House compliance follow-up (£231M flagged — 3 overdue, 1 dissolved, 3 insolvency-history)
strategic_themes.rationale: Companies House lookup on top-50 suppliers identified £231M of spend with statutory-compliance flags: £110M to suppliers with overdue accounts (3), £9M to dissolved-status companies (1), £111M to companies with insolvency history (3). NOTE: Some matches are CH fuzzy-search false positives (e.g. school, government-body name collisions) and need human verification. After verification, real flags = (a) credit-risk review on overdue accounts, (b) contract-cleanup on dissolved entities (records still on ledger but supplier extinct — risk of duplicate-payment leakage), (c) PCR 2015 Reg.57 discretionary exclusion review on insolvency-history suppliers in active contracts.

strategic_themes.title: Refund / credit-note management + contract dispute resolution (£17M, 1,267 rows)
strategic_themes.rationale: 1,267 negative-amount rows totalling £17M — refunds, credit notes, contract reversals. Volume signals correct ledger capture, but proactive levers exist: (a) contract management review on top recurring refund counterparties, (b) duplicate-payment pre-detection, (c) energy-bill credit-management automation. Typical 5-10% reduction in refund volume + faster reconciliation = 10-30bp net cash improvement.
strategic_themes.decision_owner: Head of Procurement + Internal Audit + Treasury

strategic_themes.title: Audit + recover £118M in flagged duplicate-payment patterns
strategic_themes.rationale: DOGE forensic flagged £118M across 7,170 groups of likely duplicates. Industry recovery norm 5-15% via duplicate-detection software (AP Forensics, FISCAL, Oracle Concur). Lloyds Bank Commercial Card analysis typical for spot-check sample of 100 highest-confidence matches.

strategic_themes.title: Investigate £9M in flagged split-payment patterns
strategic_themes.rationale: DOGE flagged £9M across 0 split-payment instances. Split payments often indicate (a) below-procurement-threshold ledger fragmentation circumventing PCR 2015 Reg.4 contract-value-aggregation rule; or (b) legitimate sub-line invoice splits. Sample audit + reclassify; misuse triggers Reg. 99 challenge exposure.
